### Contributing guidelines

- [x] I have read [CONTRIBUTING.md](https://github.com/nvim-mini/mini.nvim/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md)
- [x] I have read [CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md](https://github.com/nvim-mini/mini.nvim/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md)

### Module(s)

new

### Description

**Description**
I'd like to request a unified setup configuration similar to other Neovim plugin distributions like _snacks.nvim_, where modules can be enabled/disabled and configured through a single setup call.

**Current Behavior**
Currently, each Mini module requires individual setup calls:
```lua
require("mini.ai").setup({})
require("mini.files").setup({})
require("mini.comment").setup({})
-- etc.
```

**Desired Behavior**
A unified configuration interface that allows enabling/disabling modules and setting their options in one place:
```lua
require("mini").setup({
  ai = { enabled = true, opts = {} },
  files = { enabled = true, opts = { windows = { preview = true } } },
  comment = { enabled = true, opts = {} },
  surround = { enabled = false }, -- disabled module
  -- ... other modules
})
```

**Use Case Example**
This approach is successfully implemented in plugins like _snacks.nvim_:
```lua
return {
  "folke/snacks.nvim",
  opts = {
    bigfile = { enabled = true },
    dashboard = { enabled = true },
    image = { enabled = true },
    input = { enabled = true },
    notifier = { enabled = true, timeout = 3000 },
    -- ... other modules
  },
}
```

**Benefits**
1. Cleaner configuration - Single setup call instead of multiple requires
2. Explicit control - Clearly see which modules are enabled/disabled
3. Consistent pattern - Follows established patterns in the Neovim ecosystem
4. Easier maintenance - All configuration in one structured object

I'm migrating from using individual Mini modules to the unified _mini.nvim_ repository and would love to have this streamlined configuration approach.
Would this be feasible to implement? I'd be happy to help test or provide more details if needed.

comment_data.body:
Thanks for the suggestion!

The 'mini.nvim' is designed for each module to be independent both in its code and setup. Having a single `require('mini').setup()` is possible, of course, but goes against that approach.

On top of that, several modules export config helpers (like [`MiniAi.gen_spec`](https://nvim-mini.org/mini.nvim/doc/mini-ai.html#miniai.gen_spec) and similar) that are designed for "separate setup" approach.

So I am afraid I am going to close this as not planned.

---

> 3\. Consistent pattern - Follows established patterns in the Neovim ecosystem

If you mean "one `setup()` for a plugin" pattern, then separate `require('mini.xxx').setup()` calls follows exactly that.

---

> I'm migrating from using individual Mini modules to the unified _mini.nvim_ repository and would love to have this streamlined configuration approach.

Would you mind elaborating what benefit would a single `setup()` call introduce? If it is for 'folke/lazy.nvim' plugin manager to pick up `opts`, then using `config` field should work similarly.
